starters.ask.0: How can I help secure your application today?
starters.ask.1: Ready to strengthen your security posture.
starters.ask.2: What security challenge are you facing?
starters.ask.3: Let me help you find and fix vulnerabilities.
starters.ask.4: Ask me anything about application security.
starters.ask.5: Your AI security assistant is ready.
starters.ask.6: Need help with a security issue?
starters.ask.8: I'm listening. Tell me about your security needs.
starters.ask.9: Your security matters. I am here to help.
starters.ask.10: Share your security concerns. I am all ears.
starters.ask.11: I am ready to assist with your security questions.
starters.ask.12: Tell me what is on your mind regarding security.
starters.ask.13: I am here and attentive to your security needs.
starters.ask.14: Your security questions are important to me.
starters.ask.15: I am tuned in. What security topics interest you?
starters.agent.0: I am your security engineer. Point me at a target.
starters.agent.1: Ready to run the pentest. Give me a target.
starters.agent.2: Recon first, exploitation next. Name a scope.
starters.agent.4: I will scan, fingerprint and report. Start me off.
starters.agent.5: Give me a domain and I will map its attack surface.
starters.agent.6: Let me chain recon, scanning and verification for you.
starters.agent.7: Ready to hunt vulnerabilities on your in-scope assets.
starters.agent.8: I run the tools, you get the findings. Target?
starters.agent.9: Drop a target and I will begin the engagement.
starters.agent.10: I will own the recon pass. What is in scope?
starters.agent.11: Point me at your asset and I will find the way in.
promptGroups.overview.label: Overview
promptGroups.overview.prompts.0: Summarize the security posture of this workspace
promptGroups.overview.prompts.1: Break down my security score and what is lowering it
promptGroups.overview.prompts.2: What are the top 5 risks I should fix this week?
promptGroups.overview.prompts.3: Which targets have the most assets and vulnerabilities?
promptGroups.overview.prompts.4: Write an executive security summary I can share with leadership
promptGroups.attack-surface.label: Attack surface
promptGroups.attack-surface.prompts.0: What assets are exposed in this workspace?
promptGroups.attack-surface.prompts.1: Which open ports are most common, and which ones look risky?
promptGroups.attack-surface.prompts.2: Which hosts run outdated or end-of-life technologies?
promptGroups.attack-surface.prompts.3: Find assets that expose admin panels or login pages
promptGroups.attack-surface.prompts.4: List the assets discovered for each of my targets
promptGroups.vulnerabilities.label: Vulnerabilities
promptGroups.vulnerabilities.prompts.0: Show my critical and high vulnerabilities and how to fix them
promptGroups.vulnerabilities.prompts.1: Which vulnerabilities have a known CVE?
promptGroups.vulnerabilities.prompts.2: Prioritize my vulnerabilities by severity and exposure
promptGroups.vulnerabilities.prompts.3: Explain my riskiest vulnerability with its CVSS score and a fix
promptGroups.vulnerabilities.prompts.4: Group vulnerabilities by asset so I can assign owners
promptGroups.recon.label: External recon
promptGroups.recon.prompts.0: Run an external recon pass on my in-scope domains: enumerate subdomains, crawl the live hosts to map their endpoints, collect archived URLs from public sources, then summarize the exposed attack surface
promptGroups.recon.prompts.1: Map the web attack surface of my target: crawl it to depth 3, gather historical paths, and fuzz the top forms to find hidden parameters
promptGroups.recon.prompts.2: Find hidden directories and files on my web asset using a common wordlist, and flag anything that looks like an admin panel, backup or config file
promptGroups.recon.prompts.3: Fingerprint the technologies behind my live host so I can choose the right next steps for it
promptGroups.recon.prompts.4: Check my public web asset and build repositories for leaked credentials and API keys, then report what to rotate
promptGroups.ports.label: Ports & services
promptGroups.ports.prompts.0: Scan my public host for open ports, then fingerprint the services on what is open and report what is unexpectedly exposed to the internet
promptGroups.ports.prompts.1: Run a full TCP scan, fingerprint the service versions, and list any service that is end-of-life or outdated
promptGroups.ports.prompts.2: Compare my open ports against the previous scan and highlight new or changed services since then
promptGroups.ports.prompts.3: Report which non-web services are exposed to the internet, and whether those services require authentication
promptGroups.ports.prompts.4: Check my public-facing host for exposed admin panels, debug pages and default installations
promptGroups.web-scan.label: Web app pentest
promptGroups.web-scan.prompts.0: Run a vulnerability scan with the critical and high severity templates, then summarize the findings with a fix for each
promptGroups.web-scan.prompts.1: Baseline scan for common web misconfigurations and rank the results by severity
promptGroups.web-scan.prompts.2: Scan my web asset for outdated components and known-vulnerable libraries, and report what to upgrade
promptGroups.web-scan.prompts.3: Test my web server for TLS misconfigurations, missing security headers and exposed config or backup files
promptGroups.web-scan.prompts.4: Review the APIs exposed by my site for broken authentication and authorization, and report what needs fixing
